== Original post ==

'''White Slavery done RIGHT'''
* '''Author:''' Brian "HuntaWarya" Hunter
* '''Published:''' October 25, 2006
* '''Rating:''' 4.97
* '''Description:''' This is the Watto deck that helped me to a 1st place finish on Day 2 of the 2006 World Championships. It went 3-0.

=== Strategy ===

Why Watto for Day 2?  I don't know, it didn't really make a lot of sense.  But this version of Watto just kept wrecking my light decks in playtesting, so I figured it must be good.  The deck has relatively low damage potential.  It drains for very little.  But it is so solid at the Tatooine sites that you can normally start slipping in 2 damage with your objective toward the end of the game, once they can no longer afford to save 2 force during your turn.  This deck is surprisingly flexible and perhaps even more surprisingly resilient.  It has the capacity to put early pressure on the opponent, but is versatile enough to adapt to whatever game situation the opponent has created for you.  It is hard to imagine a scenario in which this deck is left with no options.

Starting Effects:

The only Effect that the deck always starts is Combat Response.  Against any deck that does not give you the Tatooine System, you will also start Kuat Drive Yards.  3rd effect can vary according to matchup.  Against decks that give you little force to start (e.g. TRM or HB), you will start Endor Shield so that with Ozzel you can flip for free.  Against a deck that gives you a lot of icons to start (e.g. EBO or LS Combat), you can skip Endor Shield, and instead start Crossfire to help you get the Occupation running faster.  Lastly, in a matchup against WHAP, I actually skipped both the Endor Shield AND Crossfire, electing to start Imperial Decree.  This is an option you could also consider against MBO.

Rule #1:  Pull your first Watto from reserve deck, even if you have one in your opening draw.  You don't want to activate your remaining two Wattos when trying to deploy him from reserve if the first one dies.  And as long as you pull your first Watto from reserve deck, your opponent might try paying the 8 to put him in your used pile, hoping you haven't drawn into a 2nd copy.

Rule #2:  Lightsaber-wielding characters that you pull with Blizzard 4 are intended to defend Watto at the Junkyard, not defend Mos Espa.  Let Sidious or Blizzard 4 defend Mos Espa.  It isn't as important as the Junkyard.  Make the Junkyard a fortress first, then worry about Mos Espa.

Rule #3:  Get a jump on the Tatooine system.  This deck is not for the faint of heart.  You have to take chances sometimes, whether it means leaving watto alone without a Ghhhk, or deploying Zuckuss on the Mist Hunter with no barrier and no backup.  This deck MUST NOT pay for Battle Plan.  Get your wookie in space, come hell or high water.  The deck is designed so that you can often deploy a ship to Tatooine, and flip your objective, and drop the Occupation, all on turn 1.  If you have the cards, DO IT, against anything but the most seriously dedicated of LS ground beats decks.

Rule #4:  Once you deploy Blizzard 4, don't forget to have Ozzel board as a passenger.  His 3 power is usually not as good as his 4 forfeit.

Rule #5:  The Tatooine system is Premiere.  Maul usually won't be in space to drain +1 there.  But you'll usually have ships there to provide you with a power bonus in the many, MANY battles that will soon be taking place at your sites.

Card Choices:

Barrier x3? - Traditionally Imperial Barrier wasn't that outstanding of a card for Watto decks to use at the Junkyard.  You still had to battle the character they deployed sooner or later, and that character was still going to hit Watto with a weapon most likely.  But Dr. E/Disarmed changes all of that.  Imperial Barrier is massive when you have Dr. Evazan at the Junkyard.  It is also big when the TIE Cannons face the X-Wing Cannons.  Shooting first is everything.

Tatooine/Occupation instead of Mob Points/Rendili - This is all about damage potential.  Watto decks don't usually force drain for a lot unless they use Blaster Racks.  Occupation makes up for the missing damage, as well as the Tatooine System proving a power bonus at your sites.  This is worth paying 2 force for Kuat Drive Yards, in my opinion.

Bridge - Deck just doesn't activate much.  Sure, you will deploy some cards for free, but I will happily accelerate for the bridge whenever I get the chance.

MM/EO - Savrip is only moderately annoying for this deck, but having a way to cancel it is better than not.  TIE cannons are good for disrupting Celebrations on Tatooine or Cloud City, but this card gives you a nice Plan B.  Finally, Watto is so susceptible to battle damage in the early game that I think running a Ghhhk is mandatory.  This card gives you an extra way to bring the Ghhhk to your hand.

Grand Moff Tarkin - Once the Endor Shield grabs Ozzel for your speedy flip, you can use Blizzard 4 to bust out Vader, and Endor Shield to pull Tarkin.  Vader/Tarkin/Watto at the Junkyard, with Ozzel on Blizzard 4 at Mos Espa, is VERY easy to set up reliably with this deck.

Blizzard 4 x3 - Call me crazy, but I think Blizzard 4 is just plain spectacular in Watto decks, and this idea could revolutionalize the way Watto decks are built for a long time to come.  Blizzard 4 is a monolith at Mos Espa, while giving you Vader or Jade to sit next to Watto.  How much better does it get?  And Blizzard 4 + Crossfire + power bonus from Tatooine system (even if it is only +2) is really not to be trifled with, even by a big gun like Mace Windu himself.  But ultimately, the Junkyard is SO tough to tangle with, that fighting Blizzard 4 becomes the more attractive option by default.  And once they lose a few cards (or a jedi) to battle damage, in order to get rid of the Big Blue Machine, you just deploy another one.  Trust me, by the time you deploy the third copy of Blizzard 4 in the same game, your opponent is going to be rolling his eyes so hard he'll be in danger of falling out of his chair.

Maul's Sith Infiltrator - I would really rather play two EPP Maul and zero copies of Tatooine Maul, BUT, Tatooine Maul + The Infiltrator is just so money against HB that you almost have to play it.  Throw in Security Precautions, and Search & Destroy, and you have a very legitimate shot against the vast majority of HB decks.

Luke, Luuuuke (v) - Defense against LS Combat.  Your Dark Jedi can't drain on Tatooine, but with Tatooine Occupation, and Luke Luke (v), you should jump ahead in the damage race enough to force the Jedi to come to you, instead of sending your Dark Jedi to Naboo.  2x Control helps defend this effect from Alter.

Weapon Levitation - As long as Vader or Jade is always next to Watto (and as long as LS Epps are out of favor), this card is usually better than Force Field.  It can also be used to help find the TIE Cannons easier.

Elis Helrot - This is your last-ditch effort card against Combat, if you've been unable to force them to your turf.  During activate phase, send Maul and the Doctor to Naboo, and as the first action in your control phase, Disarm and Operate.  Then either drain 3 at the Core, or cross your fingers and battle whoever is still standing.

Combat Readiness - As mentioned in the Senate deck, this card is just plain mean when combined with Set for Stun or the TIE Cannons.

Control/Set For Stun - Primarily here to cancel Sense if used against your Barriers.  But also combos well with Combat Readiness to bounce key pilots in space.  Can also be used to rid yourself of pesky Sandwhirls on Tatooine, or even just to cancel Imperial Atrocity if you are hellbent on forcing the Occupation damage through.

Broken Concentration - Might randomly slow down some jedi tests.  But in most matchups, just forces your opponent to conserve 4 force for your turn rather than 2.  Doesn't sound like a big deal, but it can be.

I've Lost Artoo! - Same as in the Dark Senate.  Put some of your lower-destiny interrupts under the Starting Effect, and you can save cardslots while improving your destiny average.  This deck and the Senate deck both pull enough cards in the early game to warrant the use of Fear is My Ally over Drop (v).

Options for Card #61:

Ability, Ability, Ability (v)

Cold Feet (v)

2nd Zuckuss (v)

2nd EPP Maul (3rd Maul overall)

Matchups you like to see:

QMC, WYS Raiders, MWYHL, WHAP, Profit, RST

Matchups you don't like to see:

HB,(though the Security Precautions/Tatooine Maul/Infiltrator package gives you a better chance against HB than most Watto decks would have) EBO, LS Senate, Hyperdrive and TRM

Matchups that could go either way:

TIGIH, Combat

Thanks for Reading
